stem: Ate Mila buys 2.5 kilograms of pork at ₱320 per kilogram. How much does she pay?
hints: Multiply the price per kilogram by the number of kilograms: ₱320 × 2.5.
₱320 × 2 = ₱640. ₱320 × 0.5 is half of ₱320. Add the two parts.

solution.methodName: Multiply by a decimal: split it into easy parts

steps.action: Cost = price per kilogram × number of kilograms = ₱320 × 2.5.

steps.why: 0.5 is one half, which is easy to work with by hand.
Multiplying by 0.5 is the same as taking half.

trapNotes.₱640: This is the price of only 2 kilograms. Do not forget the extra 0.5 kilogram.
trapNotes.₱80: This puts the decimal point one place too far left (₱320 × 0.25). 2.5 kg must cost more than 2 kg, which is ₱640.
trapNotes.₱8,000: This is 320 × 25. It drops the decimal point in 2.5.
